messages:
Ryan Patel: FYI sales dropped a compliance ask from a POC customer. ACME wants 7-year audit log retention + SOC2 evidence export. They've attached a questionnaire PDF and want confirmation by EOW.
Maria Gomez: tagging @niya — can security confirm feasibility and any blockers?
Niya Singh: quick take: 7 years is fine technically but raises storage/cost and legal review for EU data. Also need clarity on what counts as 'audit log' (request/response bodies? ip addresses?).
Sam Ortiz: ACME is in late-stage negotiation, legal asked for retention language in contract. sales says this is a gating item for a dedicated deal.
Alex Chen: sounds like product-scope + infra cost. Need to know whether retention is per-customer toggle vs global policy. Also export format — do they want raw logs or SOC2-style packaged evidence?
Niya Singh: list of items we need from them to triage: 1) exact retention scope (logs, payloads, metadata) 2) jurisdiction (EU/US) 3) format needed (CSV/JSON/SIEM/syslog) 4) encryption/tenant-keying requirements 5) ACL/audit access expectations.
Ryan Patel: Sales supplied this snippet from the questionnaire:```json
{
  "question": "Do you retain request/response logs?",
  "desired_retention_years": 7,
  "evidence_format": "downloadable archive with hashes",
  "regulatory_scope": "SOC2, GDPR"
}
```
Maria Gomez: thanks. @alex can we scope a minimal launch: (A) retention toggle (metadata + headers) for 7y, (B) export endpoint for zipped evidence with checksum, (C) opt-in tenant-managed KMS later? proposal: implement A+B as MVP, C in next quarter.
Alex Chen: technically A is quick if we store logs in S3 with lifecycle policy and tagging per-tenant. B requires a jobs pipeline to assemble signed archives + manifest. Rough estimate: 2 sprints for infra + 1 sprint for API + docs.
Niya Singh: security caveats: if request/response bodies include PII we need redaction or legal/DSR workflows. For EU customers GDPR may prevent long retention unless lawful basis exists — need legal. Also key-management: if they want tenant-side KMS, we need design and mTLS for key exchange.
Sam Ortiz: sales says ACME will accept metadata-only retention as interim if we can commit to export later. They prefer a roadmap milestone they can sign against.
compliance-bot: Created ticket PROD-4281: "Audit log retention & export for ACME" assigned to @alex. Link: https://redwood.infra/issue/PROD-4281
Maria Gomez: OK next steps: 1) @alex draft implementation plan + cost estimate by Tue 2) @niya list security requirements and must-have gating items by Tue 3) @sam confirm ACME accepts metadata-only interim option and get legal contact. If all green we'll add to upcoming sprint and mark as "sales-driven priority".
Alex Chen: I'll draft plan. preliminary question: do we centralize retention policy UI per-tenant or provide API-only? lean to API-first and add console toggle after.
Niya Singh: API-first ok. I'll add redaction checklist and required contract language snippets for legal.
Sam Ortiz: pinging sales to confirm interim options and ask for legal rep.
Ryan Patel: thanks all. please update PROD-4281 with notes & attach their questionnaire PDF.
Maria Gomez: can we set tentative target: feature flag rollout to staging in 4 weeks, beta with ACME in 6 weeks, GA in 10-12 weeks depending on legal. :calendar:
Alex Chen: noted. adding rough timeline to ticket.
Niya Singh: also added: retention encryption-at-rest is non-negotiable. tenant-key option flagged as future.
Sam Ortiz: ACME legal replied — they can accept metadata-only interim but will push for full payload retention later. I'll post their legal contact in the ticket.
Ryan Patel: great. closing the loop: label PROD-4281 = sales-blocker, security-review-required.
Maria Gomez: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
